additional_info.subject: ID0397739-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Not starting charge sessions CRM:00797001602
additional_info.body:
Dear Colin Barry,
Thank you for reaching
out
to eMobility Support. My name is
Sominath
, and I will be assisting you with your following query today:
Product
: Sicharge D - Charging Center
Main Asset
:
MP / S2 170003301
ChargerID/Serial No.
:
E7gWMK
Problem Description
: The charger is not starting charge sessions and is prematurely ending charge sessions.
Troubleshooting
:
1st issue:
We have analyzed the logs and noticed that the charger sent the StartTransaction request to the OCPP backend, but the charger did not receive a response within 15 seconds. Instead, it received the response after 30 seconds, which is why this session failed. Please refer to the attached logs below for your reference.
2025-01-01T12:41:47.733100+00:00
sicharge-cp [local0:info] sicharge-cp-backend/2603128c69d5[698]: OCPP: Send command:

"stack":"Error: Timeout for message
e347a513-3c83-47b7-b920-9bbba76a0bcd - {\"connectorId\":4,\"idTag\":\"040FF3FA7E6B81\",\"meterStart\":0,\"timestamp\":\"2025-01-01T12:41:47.726Z\"}\n at onRejectResponse (/node_modules/@sicharge-cp/ocpp-lib/dist/Connection.js:212:82)\n at Timeout.<anonymous> (/node_modules/@sicharge-cp/ocpp-lib/dist/Connection.js:192:25)\n at listOnTimeout (node:internal/timers:559:17)\n at processTimers (node:internal/timers:502:7)"}
2025-01-01T12:42:17.345393+00:00
sicharge-cp [local0:err] sicharge-cp-backend/2603128c69d5[698]: Response for unknown message: [3,"e347a513-3c83-47b7-b920-9bbba76a0bcd",{"transactionId":996584342,"idTagInfo":{"status":"Accepted"}}]
Proposal to Address the Issue:
To prevent similar issues in the future, we recommend increasing the default timeout period for OCPP messages from
15 seconds
to more than
30 seconds
. This will allow the charger to wait longer for a response from the backend before terminating the session. If no response is received within the extended period, the session will still terminate.
Please let us know if we have your permission to increase the default timeout for OCPP messages to more than 30 seconds.
2nd issue:
To assist you better, could you please provide the following information:
Was this session attempted on Outlet 2?
How was the authorization processed for this session?
If you have the exact timestamp of this session, could you please provide it to us?
For future reference, your case number is
0397739
, please do refer to this in all further communication regarding this issue.
We thank you for your time and patience in advance.
With best regards,
eMobility Tech Support Team -
Sominath Nagalgaon

additional_info.body:
Colin Barry,
Thank you for the feedback.
can you confirm the time out has increased?
Yes, the 'OCPP Response Timeout' has been increased to 45 seconds.
Please advise who would have set it originally to 15 seconds and why we didnt have it set to 30 seconds before? We had an issue going back some months which meant that the software provider Fuuse said repeatedly that the charger would drop the connection to their server and this was the cause of pre authorised transactions being taken and sessions not starting. Is this what we are talking about here? are there any negatives in moving the timeout to 30 seconds? why not go to 60 seconds?
>> The preferred OCPP (Open Charge Point Protocol) response timeout typically depends on the specific implementation and use case. However, a commonly recommended response timeout for most OCPP operations is between 10 and 30 seconds.
It’s important to note that the timeout can be adjusted based on system performance, network reliability, and the type of transaction being processed. In some cases, the timeout can be set lower (e.g., 10 seconds) to enable faster communication, while in other cases, it may be set higher (e.g., 30 seconds) to accommodate network delays or backend processing times. As mentioned above, the 'OCPP Response Timeout' has now been increased to 45 seconds.
Reference problem 2
>> We kindly ask for your patience as we investigate the issue and will get back to you as soon as possible. Thank you for your understanding.
Best Regards,
Sominath Nagalgaon
eMobility Support Team

additional_info.subject: Update from Jason
additional_info.body:
We will do - we have an engineer going out in Wednesday - there are two separate issuse here
The NOC team did a firmware update to v6 last week, and the charger has not reported into SCB since then
We have problems on other Irish chargers, which <may> affect this one, or it may still be the issues after the v6 update

additional_info.subject: RE: ID0399431-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Unable to charge with card CRM:00579001400
additional_info.body:
Hi Colin,
There are two things at play here.
Firstly, I don’t have access to charger logs (common with all the Irish chargers at the moment) which we believe is a Vodafone IE issue which is being investigated. Without that access, I can’t begin to work out why your charger isn’t taking contactless payments. An engineer has been requested and will be at the site as early as possible to try and understand the issues with our modem / Vodafone IE.
Secondly, I see a number of successful transactions over the weekend – what appears not to be working is the contactless transactions – and there is no integration between the charger and the terminal – that side is all handled by Payter Cloud and Fuuse. With what I know at the moment, I do not believe it is a charger issue, but to help identify the true cause, I need to see logs.
We will know more about why I have lost logging access when the engineer arrives – hopefully tomorrow but at the latest Wednesday. But, as stated, I believe it is an issue with Vodafone since I have lost access to all my chargers in Ireland.
Until we and/or Fuuse prove otherwise, I do not believe this is a charger issue - I believe this is a contactless terminal issue, or a processing issue at Fuuse.
Thanks,
Jason

additional_info.subject: Re: ID0399431-DC/Si-D/IE-[MP / S2 170003301] Unable to charge with card CRM:00579001400

Adam / Jason,
4 hour guaranteed response by the 24/7 Indian office has been achieved to date with the two incidents but as usual, when it comes to local service we are let down. We are faced with a further long delay and customer impact.
Your critical infrastructure modem is offline. The Payter terminal is online, Payter have pushed updates to their unit and it is working.
Whether you think this is a Fuuse issue or not, there is no way to find out until you get the charger online.
No one in the UK office is available at the weekends so for a Level 1 incident such as this, its not acceptable to be telling us we have to
wait
until Wednesday.
As a critical event (no remote access / no successful customer charges) someone should have been on site on Saturday within hours of being notified, irrespective of what you say about Vodafone.
Support ultimately relies on resolution and not response. We want to see resolution of critical problems given an adequate resolution time going forwards.
Regards,
Colin

additional_info.subject: Site intervention on 1/14/2025
additional_info.body:
Checked all the settings of Router1. Scanned the operators (found Vodafone to be forbidden). Restarted connection.
Suspect either SIM or Router is not working.
To confirm the same, we need to check with spare SIM and/or spare Router.
No spare SIM was available with RC. Hence t
ried swapping the SIM from Router 2 in Router1, but that SIM (Vodafone) didn't worked in Router 1 as it was M2M.
We changed the APN setting to auto for testing.
While concluding today's activity RC rebooted charger from OCPP, after that charger was stuck on Hello Screen and were offline on OCPP as well.
We tried to ping all the components and were able to ping all.
Consulted ES team, they confirmed issue with CFAST card.
